newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks resume upward trend, close higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks resume upward trend, close higher.

text.p: Argentine blue chips Thursday resumed their upward trend on institutional buying and closed 1.24 percent higher after a decline of 1.08 percent Wednesday, dealers said.

"Institutional investors were buyers today encouraged by Latin American bonds' firmness and expectations that U.S. unemployment data to be released Friday would not prompt a U.S. rates hike," said Jorge Bonanno of broker Interfin.
Blue chip index MerVal closed at 636.58 points to an accumulated gain of 3.17 percent so far this month.
"The stock market maintains a defined upward trend, with some slight profit-taking amid very low volume, to consolidate afterwards at higher volume," Banco Francs said in a report.
Volume was $25.8 million compared to $23.4 million on Wednesday and $40 millon on Tuesday.
The broader general index rose 0.85 percent.
Gainers beat losers 40 to 12 with 19 shares flat. Biggest gainers among main tiers were paper-maker Celulosa with 4.2 percent and sugar firm Ledesma with 4.0.
"The market will need tomorrow higher liquidity levels to consolidate its gains," Bonanno said.
